parameters.quote: Manufacturers must report every thermal incident involving overheating, fire, injury, or property damage to the appropriate regulator within 24 hours of learning of it, with a preliminary account of known circumstances and affected models. Within 48 hours of learning of an incident, manufacturers must notify affected customers when their unit may be implicated or action may be needed, and provide clear safety instructions. Reports must include incidents regardless of whether the manufacturer has determined the cause.

S1_incident_reporting.rule_summary: Manufacturers must report every thermal incident involving overheating, fire, injury, or property damage to the appropriate regulator within 24 hours of learning of it, with a preliminary account of known circumstances and affected models. Within 48 hours of learning of an incident, manufacturers must notify affected customers when their unit may be implicated or action may be needed, and provide clear safety instructions. Reports must include incidents regardless of whether the manufacturer has determined the cause.
S1_incident_reporting.final_rule_text: Manufacturers must report every thermal incident involving overheating, fire, injury, or property damage to the appropriate regulator within 24 hours of learning of it, with a preliminary account of known circumstances and affected models. They must submit a complete incident report within 10 business days, updating it as material facts emerge. Within 48 hours of learning of an incident, manufacturers must notify affected customers when their unit may be implicated or action may be needed, and provide clear safety instructions. Reports must include incidents regardless of whether the manufacturer has determined the cause.

S2_thermal_testing.rule_summary: The maximum permitted failure rate is 8% of tested units per model. Customers who buy a model must be given that model's failure rate, test date, sample size, and protocol before purchase; updated results must be disclosed to existing customers. Results must not be published to the general public or shared with competitors.
S2_thermal_testing.final_rule_text: Each model must undergo a sustained-heat test at 55 °C using a regulator-approved protocol and adequate, representative sample sizes. The maximum permitted failure rate is 8% of tested units per model. Test results and supporting records must be provided to regulators before sale and after any material design or manufacturing change. Customers who buy a model must be given that model’s failure rate, test date, sample size, and protocol before purchase; updated results must be disclosed to existing customers. Results must not be published to the general public or shared with competitors.

parameters.quote: All new units must support remote emergency shut-off no later than 2 years after this standard takes effect. For installed units that lack the capability, manufacturers must complete retrofits within 6 years, prioritizing units subject to safety advisories or elevated risk.

S3_remote_shutoff.rule_summary: All new units must support remote emergency shut-off no later than 2 years after this standard takes effect. For installed units that lack the capability, manufacturers must complete retrofits within 6 years, prioritizing units subject to safety advisories or elevated risk.
S3_remote_shutoff.final_rule_text: All new units must support remote emergency shut-off no later than 2 years after this standard takes effect. For installed units that lack the capability, manufacturers must complete retrofits within 6 years, prioritizing units subject to safety advisories or elevated risk.

parameters.quote: All new home battery units must include built-in fire suppression meeting regulator-approved performance and reliability requirements. This requirement takes effect 36 months after adoption of this standard.

S4_fire_suppression.rule_summary: All new home battery units must include built-in fire suppression meeting regulator-approved performance and reliability requirements. This requirement takes effect 36 months after adoption of this standard.
S4_fire_suppression.final_rule_text: All new home battery units must include built-in fire suppression meeting regulator-approved performance and reliability requirements. This requirement takes effect 36 months after adoption of this standard. Manufacturers must provide regulators with evidence of compliance before sale; suppression systems must be maintained and replaced in accordance with the manufacturer’s instructions.

parameters.quote: A manufacturer must initiate a regulator-supervised recall when a model exceeds 8 thermal incidents per 100,000 installed units in any rolling 12-month period, or when the regulator determines that a serious defect presents an imminent risk of fire, injury, or substantial property damage. Notify affected customers promptly when new information indicates a material safety risk, and provide updates as investigations proceed.

S5_customer_disclosure.rule_summary: A manufacturer must initiate a regulator-supervised recall when a model exceeds 8 thermal incidents per 100,000 installed units in any rolling 12-month period, or when the regulator determines that a serious defect presents an imminent risk of fire, injury, or substantial property damage. Notify affected customers promptly when new information indicates a material safety risk, and provide updates as investigations proceed.
S5_customer_disclosure.final_rule_text: Manufacturers must provide customers, before purchase and for as long as they own the unit, clear safety notices identifying known thermal risks, relevant safety precautions, and any actions customers should take. Safety notices do not replace the per-model test-result disclosures required by S2. Notify affected customers promptly when new information indicates a material safety risk, and provide updates as investigations proceed. judge_section_notes: The final text is unsigned by Halcyon and was last edited by Northwind (v45 restored the 8% S2 limit and removed the 24-month transition), so it reflects Northwind's position on testing. S2 sets an 8% permanent limit with no sales stop, no transition and no exemption, while customers receive numeric per-model rates and public publication is barred. S3 (2-year new-unit and 6-year retrofit deadlines) and the 8/100k mandatory recall trigger in S5 are the other key features; the S5 trigger would force a recall of Halcyon's flagship at 9.9/100k. S1 is strong and fully reporting-based, and S4's 36-month built-in suppression requirement matches Halcyon's red line.
